# Sampling Cut-Off Effect

In MEHP Force Balance (Gusev [[Gus19](../../acknowledgements.html.md#id8)], Bernhard and Gusev [[BG25](../../acknowledgements.html.md#id12)]),
entanglements are sampled between bead pairs within a spatial cut-off
$\|\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\| \le r_{\text{cut}}$.

Two distinct physical regimes emerge as $r_{\text{cut}}$ is varied:

1. **Contact Plateau (:math:\`r_{text{cut}} lesssim 1.2 b\`)**: Only beads in direct physical
   contact are paired, leaving $G$ insensitive to small changes in $r_{\text{cut}}$.
2. **Pre-Strain Stiffening (:math:\`r_{text{cut}} gtrsim 1.5 b\`)**: Because pair counts in 3D
   scale as $P(r) \propto r^2$, mean pair separations approach $\bar{r} \approx \frac{3}{4} r_{\text{cut}}$.
   Merging distant beads into links introduces artificial pre-strain and inflates $G$
   (buffered partially when using `entanglements_as_springs=True`).

## Varying `upper_cutoff` in Entanglement Sampling

Pass `upper_cutoff` to [`sample_entanglements()`](../../api/pylimer_tools_cpp.MCUniverseGenerator.html.md#pylimer_tools_cpp.MCUniverseGenerator.sample_entanglements)
and compare rigid links (`entanglements_as_springs=False`) vs. compliant springs
(`entanglements_as_springs=True`).

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 47-68 -->
```Python
gen = pt.MCUniverseGenerator(18.0, 18.0, 18.0)
gen.set_seed(42)
gen.config_nr_of_mc_steps(0)
gen.add_strands(200, [50] * 200)
gen.add_crosslinkers(100, 4)
gen.link_strands_to_conversion(0.95)

for r_cut in (1.2, 2.6):
    es = gen.sample_entanglements(
        nr_of_entanglements_to_sample=300,
        upper_cutoff=r_cut,
        seed=f"cut_{r_cut}",
    )
    fb = gen.get_force_balance2(es, entanglements_as_springs=False)
    fb.run_force_relaxation()
    print(f"r_cut={r_cut}: sampled={len(es)}, iterations={fb.get_nr_of_iterations()}")

cache_path = get_example_cache_path("sampling_cutoff_effect_cache.npz", "force_balance")
data = load_or_compute_cache(cache_path, run_sampling_cutoff_simulation)
```

## Modulus & Initial Force Residual vs. $r_{\text{cut}}$

Increasing $r_{\text{cut}}$ inflates both the initial force residual (from merging
separated beads) and the relaxed shear modulus $G$, especially for
rigid links.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 74-78 -->
```Python
plot_cutoff_modulus_vs_rcut(data)
plot_cutoff_residual_vs_rcut(data)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 79-84 -->

## Interactions with Strand Length $N$, Conversion $p$, and Stoichiometry $r$

Longer strands ($N = 70$) amplify entanglement sensitivity relative to crosslink
elasticity, while incomplete conversion ($p = 0.82$) or stoichiometric imbalance
($r = 0.75$) reduce the active network modulus uniformly.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 84-88 -->
```Python
plot_cutoff_strand_length_interaction(data)
plot_cutoff_network_parameter_interaction(data)
```

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 89-93 -->

## Sampled Pair Distance Distribution & Solver Iterations

Sampled pair distances follow $P(r) \propto r^2$ up to $r_{\text{cut}}$,
and larger pre-strains require more relaxation iterations to converge.

<!-- GENERATED FROM PYTHON SOURCE LINES 93-96 -->
```Python
plot_cutoff_pair_distance_distribution(data)
plot_cutoff_solver_iterations(data)
```
